No evidence of supply-chain attacks or malicious behavior is present.

This file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices. The package conflicts with alternative versions (`gozen-git`, `gozen-bin`), which is a common and safe practice to avoid conflicts. Overall, the package metadata shows no signs of malicious intent or unsafe practices.

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows normal Godot/GDExtension packaging practice. The primary source is the project's own GitHub repository pinned by tag (`v0.15-beta`), and the Godot editor and export templates are downloaded from the official godotengine/godot-builds releases with pinned SHA-256 checksums. `git submodule update --init --recursive` fetches upstream submodules at build time; this is standard for Godot GDExtension projects and the submodule commits are pinned by the superproject, so it is not by itself malicious, though it does rely on the upstream repository and submodule hosts being trustworthy.

The build runs `scons` and then invokes the checksum-pinned Godot editor binary in headless mode to export the project, installing the result under `/opt/gozen` with a symlink. There are no suspicious network operations, no obfuscated or encoded commands, no `eval`/`base64`/`curl|bash` patterns, and no file operations outside the package/application scope. Installing Godot export templates into `~/.local/share/godot/export_templates` is the standard location for Godot templates. The only minor hygiene note is the `SKIP` checksum on the git source, which is expected for git/tag-based sources and is not evidence of malice.

Overall, I found no injected backdoors, data exfiltration, or supply-chain attack indicators. The package is consistent with a legitimate Godot-based application build.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>No malicious behavior found; package follows standard Godot/GDExtension AUR practices.</summary>
